cards.claim: Multi-scale augmentation (continuous resizing during training) achieves high performance without increased training time compared to single-size or curriculum learning strategies
cards.conditions: ImageNet pre-trained ResNet models fine-tuned on calcaneus fracture x-ray radiographs (1,775 images); training on images resized between 128×128 and 900×900
cards.effect: AUROC 0.938 (95% CI: 0.936–0.939) without increased training or inference time
cards.evidence: Empirical measurement of AUROC and training time across strategies
cards.quote: Multi-scale augmentation achieved the highest average area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (0.938; 95% CI: 0.936–0.939) across image resolutions without increased training or inference time.
cards.note: Tangentially relevant: shows resolution-aware training can decouple performance from training time cost

cards.claim: Curriculum learning (sequential training from low to high resolution) requires significantly longer training time despite improved sensitivity
cards.effect: Training time 11.8 hours (IQR: 11.1–16.4) with improved sensitivity (85.4%–90.1% for in-distribution, 78.2%–89.2% for out-of-distribution)
cards.evidence: Measured training time and sensitivity metrics
cards.quote: Curriculum learning demonstrated the highest sensitivity for in-distribution low-resolution images (85.4%–90.1%) and out-of-distribution high-resolution images (78.2%–89.2%) but required significantly longer training times (11.8 [IQR: 11.1–16.4] hours; P <.001).
cards.note: Shows schedule-based resolution changes increase computational cost
